rv.q: It could run and run in downtown Chicago, too.
Fields and her terrific band — including Frank Menzies on keys, Julie Poncé on bass, Harold Morrison on drums, and Ricardo Jimenez on trumpet — absolutely deliver.
If you love blues songs, then Writers Theatre's Pearl's Rollin' With The Blues: A Night With Felicia P. Fields is a dazzling Wang Dang Doodle of a night you don't want to miss.

Felicia P. Fields and Chic Street Man offer songs of love, faith, happiness and hope that are guaranteed to bring audiences to their feet, singing along, clapping their hands, stomping their feet and rejoicing that the “Blues Is All Right.”
In fact, it would be difficult to think of a more ideal, mostly laugh-inducing tonic for this moment when the world seems truly out of control.
When she makes her entrance in Rollin’ With the Blues, you know you’re in the presence of greatness, and fortunate to be there indeed.
I highly recommend that you go and get your mojo working.
A powerhouse singer whose shrewd, playful presence served her well as she bantered with the audience, Fields is enormously entertaining.
At its best, the evening offered sober consolation and an affirmation of life even in the face of pain.
Ninety minutes of pure enjoyment might be the headline for this one.
This production provides you with a great evening of entertainment, music, singing, comedy and much more!

cn.t: Critics enthusiastically celebrate this blues revue as a triumphant showcase for Tony-nominee Felicia P. Fields' powerhouse vocals and magnetic stage presence, with praise for Ron OJ Parson's direction and the stellar musicianship.
